markdown_report:
**Proposed direction: audit negative coverage before changing NextItNet’s loss.** At 20% progress, retain this diagnostic extension, but distinguish sampler accessibility, optimizer exposure, and objective-specific gradient quality.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** First, CDs has a sampled training margin of 12.03 but training-prefix catalog HR@10 of zero. Different samples and candidate universes prevent attributing this discrepancy to sampling alone. Second, permutation worsens ranks in several categories. This establishes measured order sensitivity, without establishing useful recency weighting. Third, position-preserving replacements separate context and inserted-candidate competition. Their effects remain conditional on successful matching and corruption plausibility.

**Insights from related work.** [Rank-estimation research](https://research.google/pubs/improved-estimation-of-ranks-for-learning-item-recommenders-with-negative-sampling/) motivates exact catalog anchors. [Sampling-distribution analysis](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/blanc18a.html) connects sampling to optimization bias, but coverage alone omits gradient weights and Jacobians. [Zhang and Nanda](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042) demonstrate corruption-sensitive localization; retain random and plausible replacements. Hard-negative analyses motivate controlled experiments, while false negatives remain a concern.

Three directions follow: improve intervention validity, calibrate competitor coverage, and test objective-specific optimization changes.

| Direction | Existing approach | Remaining question |
|---|---|---|
| Context | Position-preserving lag replacements | How do plausibility and matching support affect sensitivity? |
| Competition | Fixed/shared restricted catalogs | Does coverage differ from its sampling-design expectation? |
| Optimization | Sampled training margins | Do actual loss gradients represent catalog competition? |

Three atomic ideas remain worthwhile. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten.

- **Calibrated competitor audit: 4/7/5.** Originality: integrates sampling controls with interventions, but uses established estimators. Potential: distinguishes actionable hypotheses, but cannot predict validation gains by itself. Difficulty: reuses scoring, but sampler fidelity and paired uncertainty require care.
- **Residual restoration patching: 6/7/6.** Originality: adapts established patching to causal convolutions. Potential: localizes sensitivity, but hybrid activations may be unnatural. Difficulty: avoids retraining, but needs architecture-specific hooks [Zhang and Nanda].
- **Bounded multi-negative loss: 3/6/4.** Originality: provides a direct intervention with substantial precedent. Potential: broadens competition, but risks false-negative pressure. Difficulty: preserves inference, but increases training cost [sampled-softmax analysis](https://wujcan.github.io/papers/tois-ssm.pdf).

**Selected algorithm.** Freeze each category model and reuse deterministic training-prefix pairs. For identical eligible negatives E, define strict outrankers H and sampled unique negatives S. Report coverage |S∩H|/|H|, expected coverage from inclusion probabilities, and their ratio. Keep zero-outranker coverage undefined. Separate negative-conditional softmax coverage from target-inclusive mass; neither represents BCE/BPR gradient quality.

```text
freeze model; preregister protocol and seed 42
for clean/replacement pair:
    fix catalogs; repeat exact sampler with shared draws
    stream ranks, outrankers, masses and inclusion baselines
    retain multiplicities; measure actual-loss gradient weights
aggregate paired differences within users on common support
bootstrap users within categories; recompute four-category macro
```

Report matching exclusions, zero-outranker transitions, sampling Monte Carlo variation, and score scale. Fresh draws measure current accessibility; historical exposure requires training logs. Diagnostics remain in-sample and exploratory. One NextItNet checkpoint per category and unchanged host macro validation HR@10 govern adoption.

idea.description: Extend the existing position-preserving NextItNet intervention adapter with a sampling-design-calibrated, objective-specific competitor audit. Separate current sampler accessibility, actual historical exposure when logged, and gradient weighting; compare clean and matched replacement contexts without fitting additional predictors.
idea.motivation: Strong sampled-negative training margins coexist with weak eligible-catalog training-prefix ranking in the supplied diagnostics, but these measurements use different samples and candidate universes. The discrepancy motivates a paired audit on identical examples rather than establishing a negative-sampling failure. Qualitative complaints motivate context hypotheses but do not establish compatibility, ownership, unmet need, or present intent. At 20% research progress, this diagnostic is more feasible than architecture-specific patching and better justified than immediately adopting harder negatives.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve exactly one independently trained NextItNet model/checkpoint per category, all four dataset routes, the corrected cold start, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. No ensembles, extra datasets, pretrained weights, hidden test access, evaluator changes, or checkpoints from other trials. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), view.model, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data interfaces. The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B×L tensors. No inference change is required; checkpoint and embedded predictor consistency remain mandatory. Retain full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five real training users per category.

Preregister max_users=12/category, at most two training cuts/user, minimum prefix length 5, window 128, ten loader batches for existing margin probes, 64 accepted diagnostic negative draws, 32 independent sampler repetitions, and 1,000 user-bootstrap repetitions. These are proposed protocol settings, not measured results. Retain the existing replacement dose, lag-bin, matching, and plausibility rules verbatim in the serialized protocol; log their realized replacement IDs, positions, failure reasons, and sampling seeds. Use a dedicated diagnostic RNG seeded 42, save and restore Python/NumPy/PyTorch RNG states and individual module modes in finally, and run the frozen model in eval mode. Do not consume the training RNG stream. Construct inputs solely from training prefixes, excluding the target occurrence and subsequent interactions. Preserve occupied positions and terminal items, gather the maximum nonpadding index, and exclude empty histories; never use count-1.

For each prefix, freeze candidate eligibility from its entire original observed prefix, including interactions outside the model window. Retain the target once and exclude PAD. Define target-free eligible negatives E, strict outrankers H={i in E:s_i>s_target}, and ties separately. Exact rank is 1+|H|+the number of tied eligible negatives with lower item ID. Evaluate both the fixed catalog and the shared restricted catalog excluding inserted replacement IDs, except the target. Record restricted-catalog changes and inserted-item gains separately. Encode each variant once and stream item scores using stable logsumexp; preserve existing exhaustive synthetic rank and tie checks, identity controls, padding controls, causality checks, applicable unreachable-position controls, and replacement coverage accounting.

Reproduce the actual family-specific sampler, including proposals, rejection rules, accepted-draw counts, replacement policy, and duplicates. If unavailable, explicitly identify the diagnostic sampler and withhold training-sampler claims. Draw from the actual sampler before intersecting with E; do not silently renormalize it to diagnostic eligibility. Report original and retained draw counts, unique IDs, multiplicities, excluded mass where known, and zero-probability outrankers. Reuse each realized draw across paired variants and catalog restrictions. For m independent accepted replacement draws with known q_i, inclusion probability pi_i=1-(1-q_i)^m. Uniform sampling without replacement gives pi_i=m/N on its actual sampling support. For rejection proposals g_i and acceptance a_i, accepted-draw q_i is proportional to g_i*a_i; a fixed m-proposal budget instead gives pi_i=1-(1-g_i*a_i)^m. Rejection until m unique IDs induces a different design. Weighted sampling without replacement needs design-specific inclusion probabilities; never substitute m*q_i automatically. Where probabilities are unavailable, use independent exact-sampler repetitions to estimate expected coverage and label Monte Carlo uncertainty.

For unique retained negatives S, report C_count=|S intersect H|/|H|, C0=sum_{i in H}pi_i/|H|, and C_count/C0 when defined. Empty H makes coverage and its baseline undefined; C0=0 makes the ratio undefined. Under a correctly specified sampler, C0 is the expected observed coverage, so deviations are descriptive sampling realizations rather than evidence of optimization quality. Report coverage quantiles across repeats and account for dependent inclusion events; do not construct binomial intervals across items.

At temperature 1, define C_soft=sum_{i in S}exp(s_i)/sum_{i in E}exp(s_i), p_target=exp(s_target)/(exp(s_target)+sum_{i in E}exp(s_i)), negative captured mass A=(1-p_target)*C_soft, and target-inclusive mass M=p_target+A. The previous captured-mass diagnostic corresponds to A. Report all four quantities separately; an empty S gives A=0 when the catalog denominator exists, while an empty E makes C_soft undefined. Large M can arise from a dominant target despite poor negative coverage. For an uncorrected unique-subset softmax containing the target, with identical logits, temperature 1, unit loss weight and gradients embedded in the full item-coordinate space, full-versus-subset logit-gradient L1 discrepancy is exactly 2*(1-M). This identity does not apply unchanged to multiplicity-weighted or sampling-corrected losses, nor establish parameter-gradient alignment or ranking gains.

Identify the actual training objective and its reductions from the supplied implementation. Report negative gradient weights for BCE sigmoid(s_i), BPR sigmoid(s_i-s_target), or the actual sampled-softmax formula, including multiplicities, positive contributions, sampling corrections and batch normalization. Unique-set coverage must not stand in for repeated optimizer contributions. On a deterministic cap of eight existing clean prefixes/category, if affordable, compare the actual sampled loss with a clearly specified catalog extension of that same objective: BCE uses the same positive term and replaces the sampled-negative mean with the eligible-negative mean; BPR replaces the sampled pairwise mean with the eligible pairwise mean; softmax uses target plus E. Preserve external coefficients and document any baseline sum reduction. If no meaningful catalog extension is available, return gradient comparison unavailable. Use autograd-enabled evaluation for this optional probe, avoid optimizer steps, and compare gradient norms, cosine and relative error for features and, where feasible, item embeddings/backbone parameters. Label this reference as an objective diagnostic, not ground-truth relevance. Report logits and embedding/feature norms because score scaling changes masses and gradients while preserving ranks; score shifts affect BCE gradients but preserve BPR/softmax gradients. Any normalization remains diagnostic-only.

Fresh post-training draws measure current sampler accessibility, not cumulative exposure. Historical claims require actual context-negative occurrence logs, multiplicities, and contemporaneous scores/gradient weights where available. Without logs, report historical exposure unavailable; do not reconstruct it from the final model. The cumulative inclusion formula 1-product_t(1-q_i,t) requires independent draws with predetermined probabilities; adaptive training requires conditional analysis or logs.

Define each paired estimand on identical user-prefix observations where the required replacement procedures succeed and both compared metrics exist. Average paired differences within users before averaging users within category. Report eligible and retained users/prefixes, support rates, and retained/excluded history-length and training-frequency summaries. Complete-case effects describe retained support; do not claim population effects or apply unsupported selection weights. Separate replacement failure from structural undefinedness. Report zero-to-zero, zero-to-positive, positive-to-zero and positive-to-positive outranker transitions; rank and outranker-count differences use all successfully matched pairs, while coverage differences require jointly nonempty H.

Average inner sampler repetitions within each prefix. Bootstrap users independently within categories, retaining each user's prefixes and paired observations, and recompute equal-weight four-category macros only when every category has defined support. Report user-bootstrap intervals conditional on the stored diagnostic draws and a separate within-prefix Monte Carlo summary; inner repetitions are not extra users. Do not add Monte Carlo variance again if using a nested resampling alternative. Keep sampler-randomization repeats independent of any draws used to estimate an unavailable inclusion baseline. Preserve raw records so estimates can be recomputed.

Return metrics, metric_definitions, valid denominators, failures, unavailable reasons, protocol and synchronized elapsed cost. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; unavailable reviews, ratings, item categories/prices/stores and simulator traits remain null or empty. All diagnostic and failed-run cost counts against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget; optional gradients are omitted with a reason if unaffordable. These audits do not train shortcuts themselves, but repeated diagnosis-driven selection can overfit validation, favor popularity or encourage last-item dependence. Any subsequent single-model loss change requires a preregistered comparison under the unchanged host macro validation HR@10, with training-popularity and history-length diagnostics. No validation improvement, causal intent or generalizable user benefit is claimed here.
idea.pseudocode:
Record protocol, exact sampler semantics, objective/reduction, seeds, replacement rules, sample caps and budget cap.
Save individual module modes and Python/NumPy/PyTorch RNG states.
try:
  Freeze the category's single NextItNet; enter eval mode.
  Reuse deterministic training-prefix/next-training-target pairs.
  For each prefix:
    Build clean and matched recent/older replacement plans without shifting positions.
    Record matching success, failure reasons, replacement IDs and retained/excluded strata.
    Freeze full-original-prefix eligibility; retain target once; exclude PAD.
    Build fixed and shared restricted catalogs; define target-free eligible negatives E.
    Encode each successful variant once under no_grad.
    Gather maximum nonpadding index; exclude empty histories.
    Stream exact scores, strict outrankers H, ID-tiebroken rank, ties and logsumexp.
    For 32 independently seeded repetitions:
      Draw 64 accepted negatives using the exact sampler, preserving duplicates.
      Share the realized draw across variants and catalog restrictions.
      Intersect unique IDs with E; retain multiplicities and exclusion counts.
      Obtain design-correct pi_i, or separately estimate the sampling baseline.
      If H is nonempty:
        C_count = |S intersect H| / |H|
        C0 = sum(pi_i for i in H) / |H|
        ratio = C_count / C0 if C0 > 0 else null
      Else:
        C_count, C0, ratio = null, null, null
      Compute C_soft, p_target, negative mass A and target-inclusive mass M stably.
      Record actual-loss gradient weights, reductions, score scale and multiplicities.
    Record inserted-item gains and zero-outranker transition classes.
    Form paired differences only on metric-specific common support.
  If affordable and the objective is known:
    Enable autograd on up to eight fixed clean prefixes.
    Compare actual sampled-loss gradients with the documented catalog extension.
    Never step an optimizer or modify the checkpoint.
  Average sampler repetitions within prefixes and paired differences within users.
  Bootstrap users within category with 1,000 repetitions, retaining paired records.
  Report support, complete-case limitations and separate sampler Monte Carlo summaries.
finally:
  Restore all saved module modes and RNG states.
Return metrics, metric_definitions, raw observations, unavailable reasons and measured cost.
Aggregate equal-weight macro summaries only after all four category results exist.
Interpret fresh draws as current accessibility; historical exposure requires actual training logs.
Select any later single-model change only through unchanged pinned host macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: Connects position-preserving context interventions, candidate-insertion controls, inclusion-probability calibration and objective-specific gradient diagnostics within the NextItNet adapter.
originality.negative: The underlying coverage estimators, sampling formulas, gradient calculations and cluster bootstrap are established; this is primarily a careful diagnostic integration.

future_potential.positive: Can distinguish current sampling accessibility from loss weighting and context sensitivity, supporting smaller and better justified single-model optimization experiments.
future_potential.negative: Neither calibrated coverage nor catalog-reference gradients have an established predictive relationship with this benchmark's validation HR@10; false negatives and selection bias remain.

code_difficulty.positive: Existing prefix sampling, replacements, exact chunked scoring and aggregation provide substantial reusable infrastructure, with no required predictor change.
code_difficulty.negative: Exact sampler reproduction, inclusion probabilities, multiplicities, metric-specific paired support, uncertainty decomposition and optional gradient comparisons are materially more complex than the original coverage-only proposal.

related_work.title: Improved Estimation of Ranks for Learning Item Recommenders with Negative Sampling
contributions: Analyzes rank estimation under negative sampling and motivates anchoring sampled comparisons to exact catalog ranks.
limitations: Does not establish that insufficient competitor coverage causes the supplied NextItNet failures or predicts validation gains.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: Shows that corruption methods and evaluation metrics influence intervention-based localization.
limitations: Requires adaptation to NextItNet; sensitivity and restoration do not establish recommendation relevance.

related_work.title: Sampled-softmax analysis (2024; supplied reference)
contributions: Motivates caution about excessively hard negatives and their gradient influence.
limitations: Provides no benchmark-specific evidence that broader or harder negative training improves the four-category task.

related_work.title: Adaptive Sampled Softmax with Kernel Based Sampling
contributions: Studies sampling distributions and sampled-softmax optimization, supporting objective-specific analysis beyond unique competitor coverage.
limitations: Its softmax analysis does not directly characterize BCE or BPR gradients or establish ranking gains for the supplied model.

related_work.title: Hard-negative theory (supplied reference)
contributions: Connects hard-sampled BPR with partial-AUC and top-K objectives under the analyzed setting.
limitations: Does not imply that frozen-model coverage predicts validation HR@10 or eliminate false-negative risk.

related_work.title: Loss analysis (supplied reference)
contributions: Supports distinguishing loss formulations, including the equivalence of one-negative uncorrected softmax and BPR.
limitations: Equivalence depends on the stated formulation and does not extend automatically to corrections, multiplicities or different reductions.

related_work.title: Inclusion probabilities: survey-sampling methods
contributions: Provides inclusion-probability foundations used to derive expected unique outranker coverage.
limitations: The coverage normalization is an application proposed here; weighted and adaptive samplers require their actual design.

related_work.title: Monte Carlo notes: rejection sampling
contributions: Provides conditioning principles for deriving accepted-draw probabilities under rejection sampling.
limitations: Accepted-draw, fixed-proposal-budget and duplicate-rejection procedures induce different inclusion designs.

related_work.title: Cluster-bootstrap methods (supplied reference)
contributions: Supports resampling clusters to preserve dependence among observations from the same user.
limitations: Bootstrap intervals do not correct matching selection, small-support instability or repeated validation selection.

related_work.title: Selection-bias analysis (supplied reference)
contributions: Motivates explicit retained-population estimands and scrutiny of selection assumptions and positivity.
limitations: Does not justify population weighting without defensible selection assumptions and adequate support.

related_work.title: Nested variance estimation (supplied reference)
contributions: Motivates separating sampling Monte Carlo variation from between-user uncertainty and avoiding variance double counting.
limitations: The appropriate variance procedure depends on the implemented sampling hierarchy and estimand.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Analyzes discrepancies between sampled recommendation metrics and their full-catalog counterparts.
limitations: Repeated candidate draws improve precision for a sampled estimand without converting it into catalog ranking or changing the authoritative host evaluator.
